generic: efgartigimod alfa (VYVGART: efgartigimod alfa-fcab, IV; VYVGART Hytrulo: efgartigimod alfa and hyaluronidase-qvfc, SC)
route: Intravenous infusion (VYVGART); subcutaneous injection (VYVGART Hytrulo, approved 2023-06-20)
dosing: IV: 10 mg/kg (1,200 mg if 120 kg or more) once weekly for 4 weeks per cycle, later cycles based on clinical evaluation. SC Hytrulo: gMG 1,000 mg (prefilled syringe) or 1,008 mg (vial) once weekly for 4 weeks per cycle; CIDP once weekly continuously.
first_us_indication: Generalized myasthenia gravis in adults who are anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody positive
other_us_indications: generalized myasthenia gravis, AChR antibody positive adults, subcutaneous VYVGART Hytrulo (BLA 761304) 2023-06-20; chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy in adults (VYVGART Hytrulo) 2024-06-21; generalized myasthenia gravis expanded to AChR antibody seronegative adults (both products) 2026-05-08
notes: Sales line Product net sales combines VYVGART and VYVGART Hytrulo (and all countries). Dates from Drugs@FDA (openFDA) and FDA letters: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2023/761304orig1s000ltr.pdf ; https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2024/761304Orig1s005,s006ltr.pdf ; https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2026/761195Orig1s016; 761304Orig1s018ltr.pdf . Efficacy-class supplements of 2024-08-08, 2025-04-10 (Hytrulo prefilled syringe) and 2025-10-17 were labelling or presentation changes, not new indications. No UC or CD indication. No change in reporting company.

dosing: Thin layer twice daily to affected areas (up to 20% body surface area in atopic dermatitis, up to 10% in vitiligo); short-term, non-continuous use in atopic dermatitis.
first_us_indication: Short-term and non-continuous chronic treatment of mild to moderate atopic dermatitis in non-immunocompromised patients 12 years and older whose disease is not adequately controlled with topical prescription therapies
other_us_indications: nonsegmental vitiligo in patients 12 years and older 2022-07-18; atopic dermatitis expanded to children 2 to 11 years 2025-09-18
notes: Letters: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2022/215309Orig1s001ltr.pdf ; https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2025/215309Orig1s007ltr.pdf . The 2021 approval letter was reissued as a corrected letter giving the effective date 2021-09-21. First ex-US approval: European Commission, vitiligo, April 2023 (Incyte 10-Q Q3 2023); Incyte sells it in Europe itself. No UC or CD indication. No change in reporting company.

dosing: 23.7 mg twice daily, with mycophenolate mofetil and corticosteroids.
first_us_indication: Active lupus nephritis in adults, in combination with a background immunosuppressive therapy regimen
notes: The 2024-04-29 efficacy supplement (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2024/213716Orig1s004ltr.pdf) added long-term data supporting use beyond one year; it is not a new indication. Otsuka holds a licence (December 2020) for Europe, Japan and other markets and buys LUPKYNIS supply from Aurinia under an August 2022 supply agreement; those supply sales are inside Aurinia's product sales line. No UC or CD indication.

first_us_indication: Plaque psoriasis, including intertriginous areas, in patients 12 years and older (cream 0.3%)
other_us_indications: plaque psoriasis expanded to patients 6 to 11 years (cream 0.3%) 2023-10-05; seborrheic dermatitis in patients 9 years and older (foam 0.3%, NDA 217242) 2023-12-15; mild to moderate atopic dermatitis in patients 6 years and older (cream 0.15%) 2024-07-09; plaque psoriasis of the scalp and body in patients 12 years and older (foam 0.3%) 2025-05-22; mild to moderate atopic dermatitis in children 2 to 5 years (cream 0.05%) 2025-10-04; plaque psoriasis expanded to patients 2 years and older (cream 0.3%) 2026-06-29
notes: Letters: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2023/215985Orig1s002ltr.pdf ; https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2023/217242Orig1s000ltr.pdf ; https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2024/215985Orig1s007ltr.pdf ; https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2025/217242Orig1s005ltr.pdf ; https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2025/215985Orig1s012ltr.pdf ; https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2026/215985Orig1s015ltr.pdf . dosing: Thin layer once daily to affected areas.
first_us_indication: Topical treatment of plaque psoriasis in adults
other_us_indications: atopic dermatitis in adults and children 2 years and older 2024-12-12
notes: Ownership change: Organon acquired Dermavant; the deal closed on 2024-10-28 (Organon Q4 2024 release; Roivant 10-Q for the quarter ended December 31, 2024). dosing: Prurigo nodularis: 60 mg first dose, then 30 mg every 4 weeks (under 90 kg) or 60 mg every 4 weeks (90 kg or more). Atopic dermatitis: 60 mg first dose, then 30 mg every 4 weeks; 30 mg every 8 weeks after week 16 for patients with clear or almost clear skin.
other_us_indications: moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis in patients 12 years and older, with topical corticosteroids and/or calcineurin inhibitors (BLA 761391) 2024-12-13
notes: AD letter: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2024/761391Orig1s000ltr.pdf ; BLA 761391 was later merged into BLA 761390 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2025/761391Orig1s001,761390Orig1s002ltr.pdf).
